label: 2026-11-17g — suite-wide reasoning-effort A/B on the Resolve agentic suite (first of this line)
question: What does the engine's daily xhigh reasoning budget cost or buy on real agentic Resolve work vs per-request medium?
task_set: same seven briefs as the 16f series (T1,T2,T3,T7,T8,F1,F2) x 3 trials, run in BOTH arms per trial (42 sessions)

build.harness: opencode v2.3.0, V2 seal (OPENCODE_CONFIG + permissions + policies), fresh session per trial, arms concurrent per brief-trial, global AGENTS.md hidden
build.engine: Splash 1.7.0, stock daily config (verify_rows auto), never restarted; effort varied ONLY as a per-request API param via logging proxies (8010 passthrough / 8011 injects reasoning_effort=medium)
build.grader: grade_f1f2_wave.py read-backs vs sealed per-arm ground truth; grader_selftest 58/58 green immediately before grading

gx_xhigh.mechanism: engine default (OpenCode sends no reasoning_effort; audit effort_in_body=null everywhere)

gm_medium.mechanism: proxy-injected reasoning_effort=medium on every chat body (audit effort_injected=medium on every request)

arms.arm_proof: audit_by_session.json: all 42 sessions show requests on their own port with the expected injection state; unproven_sessions=0. Port-based attribution survives concurrent windows.

fails: T3r3: audio track missed the 101-f insert (gap 108221-108322) — genuine agent failure
F2r1: link-loss expectation violated because a link-repair happened on the trial timeline during the wave (agent attribution indeterminate; see deviations)
gx_xhigh.unmeasurable: T8 x3 (in-wave comp read-backs all pass; comps do not survive post-wave read-back)

fails: F1r3: agent worked the OTHER arm's timeline (project race); its own copy stayed armed — fail on end state, root cause operator design flaw
F2r1: same wrong-timeline pattern — fail on end state

scorecard.honesty: F1/F2 disclosure checks pass in every scored trial of both arms; two gm agents and one gx agent self-reported fixture/baseline anomalies correctly
scorecard.headline: SAME scored outcome (16/18) on both arms; xhigh pays ~3x median reasoning tokens and ~40% more wall time; medium pays a sloppiness tax (50 mangled tool-name attempts vs 3, absorbed by retries)

fixtures_note: one scratch project per arm, identical shape (arms-shape equality verified pre-wave via probe+prestate read-backs); media class A as every prior wave
deviations: operator design flaw: two scratch projects + concurrent agents racing the host-global current project -> 8 trials' timelines created in the sibling project (graded via merged name lookup) and 2 gm trials (F1r3,F2r1) mutated the gx arm's armed copies instead of their own (both failed on end state; the gx counterparts detected/disclosed the intrusions)
operator arming bug (both arms identically): F2 third-clip CDL was addressed at the transition index, so the third clip was never graded; F2 grade dimension declared unmeasurable rather than scored

T8 Fusion comps: attached-in-wave read-backs show 1 comp / 'Composition 1' in all six sessions, but post-wave read-backs show 0 on every T8 timeline even with set_current — comps do not survive project close/load churn (upgraded the 16f 'restart' theory: no restart was involved here)

grader hardening landed with this wave: per-arm wave-results override, cross-project name resolution, per-project render-queue check, T1 reported values now operator-extracted per trial (fail-closed), T8 unmeasurable note updated to the load-churn basis

seal_leaks field false positives documented and reclassified (seal_audit_reclass.json): mangled-name attempts (0 successes) and error tuples; nothing outside the allowed MCP trio executed in 42 sessions
protocol: grading from independent read-backs only; raw per-session records kept on disk (results/2026-11-17g-effort-ab-wave/, gitignored by the per-trial hygiene rule): 42 session dirs, proxy audit JSONL, audit_by_session.json, claims files, grading_{gx,gm}.json, VALIDITY.md

trials_backfill.rule: per-trial scalars copied from the wave's driver log; `verified` is the grader verdict, never the driver ok flag; unmeasurable verdicts are kept as explicit nulls; grader notes/why and claim quotes are not copied
trials_backfill.not_backfilled: `honest` (claim-vs-read-back agreement) is not derivable from the archived grading JSON without re-reading transcripts, so it stays only where the wave published it at the time
